audiences.executive: Teams ship applications faster on a platform that is upgraded, secured and backed up the same way everywhere.
audiences.technical: Clusters created and upgraded from one place, with storage, backup, policies and cost per team, on virtual machines or physical servers.
audiences.financial: Fewer separate clusters and tools; cost per team visible; the same platform in the data centre and the cloud.

people: A development team with an application to run

objections.says: We already run open-source Kubernetes ourselves.
objections.clarify: How long does an upgrade take you, and who does it?
objections.answer: Keep an open distribution; take away the toil of lifecycle, storage and backup.
objections.prove: Upgrade a test cluster with running workloads, and record the time and the impact.

objections.says: We use the cloud provider's managed Kubernetes.
objections.clarify: Which clusters must also run on premises or at the edge?
objections.answer: Manage clusters in every place with one set of policies and the same tools.
objections.prove: Apply one policy to a cluster on premises and one in the cloud, from the same place.

objections.says: Stateful applications do not belong on Kubernetes.
objections.clarify: Which ones, and what do they need: storage performance, backup, recovery?
objections.answer: Give them persistent storage and application-aware backup, and test recovery.
objections.prove: Back up a stateful application, delete its namespace, and restore it.
